prompt: A user posts a comment containing <script> and every visitor's browser runs it.
why: Untrusted text rendered as HTML runs as script. That's stored XSS.
trap: Cookies may be stolen next, but the hole is unescaped output.

prompt: The page shows the search term with innerHTML, so a crafted link runs code.
why: Writing user text as HTML enables XSS. Use textContent or escape.
trap: Nothing reaches the database; it runs in the browser.

prompt: A Content Security Policy blocks inline scripts, so injected ones don't run.
why: CSP is a second line of defence against XSS.
trap: It doesn't stop forged requests; it stops injected scripts.

prompt: The template engine escapes < and > by default, and someone turned that off for one field.
tells: turned that off for one field
why: Auto-escaping prevents XSS; disabling it reopens the hole.
trap: It's HTML escaping, not SQL escaping.

prompt: Injected script reads document.cookie and sends it to the attacker's server.
why: The injection is XSS; HttpOnly cookies would stop script from reading the session.
trap: Session theft is the goal; the way in is XSS.

prompt: Profile links allow javascript: URLs, which run when clicked.
why: A javascript: URL is script injection through an attribute. Allow only http(s).
trap: It's not a phishing page; it runs code in your site.
